headline: I was just denied a cup of sugar by my neighbor because I allegedly ‘invited the enemy’ into my living room
body:
I didn't think much of it when I knocked on Ramesh’s door yesterday morning, desperate for a few spoons of sugar to fix my tea. But before I could even explain my plight, Ramesh blocked the doorway, squinting at my entryway with the intensity of a border guard. He pointed a trembling finger at my sofa, where my brother-in-law from the neighboring housing colony—who happens to support the rival residential committee—was casually scrolling through his phone.

‘You have invited the enemy into your sanctum,’ Ramesh declared, his voice echoing through the hallway with a gravitas that felt better suited to a UN Security Council meeting. He insisted that by hosting a relative with 'ideological divergences' regarding the society’s upcoming garden fence budget, I had effectively revoked my citizenship of the building’s fourth floor. I tried to explain that we were just discussing the merits of marigolds versus roses, but Ramesh was having none of it.

He informed me that the residential bylaws clearly state that any interaction with those who hold 'subversive opinions' about our flowerbeds constitutes an act of diplomatic treason. I ended up walking three blocks to the local market, shivering under the weight of being a social pariah, all because I didn't verify the political affiliation of a man I’ve shared Sunday lunch with for fifteen years. I suppose I’ll be drinking my tea black from now on, lest I be accused of brewing a cup of sedition.
caption: Local resident faces social exile after neighbor declares a cup of sugar a high-stakes diplomatic maneuver. Politics begins at home, apparently. #SocietyDrama #SugarPolitics #DiplomaticIncident #NeighborWars (satire)
igHook: Have you ever been accused of treason just for being a polite neighbor?
